 Published  October 20, 2026 9:42 AM EDT article Photos of SpaceX's rocket launch from Florida on Oct. 20, 2026. 
 The Brief
 SpaceX launched its Bandwagon-5 mission from Cape Canaveral at 7:04 a.m. Tuesday. 
 The predawn launch created a "space jellyfish" effect that was spotted in the Florida sky. 
 Photos: Scroll down to see some of the best photos shared with FOX 35. 
 ORLANDO, Fla. - Did you see it? SpaceX launched its Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Station early Tuesday morning, which created a glowing "space jellyfish" over Central Florida.
 What is a "space jellyfish?"
 What we know:
 The "space jellyfish" happens when sunlight reflects off a rocket's exhaust plume high in the atmosphere, which creates a glowing, bulb-shaped cloud that spreads across the sky – and can be seen from miles away.
 It is most common during early morning or late evening launches.
 Best photos: ‘Space jellyfish’ over Orlando after SpaceX launch
 Local perspective:
 Several viewers were up early enough to see the rocket launch – and shared their photos with FOX 35. Click here to share yours!  
   SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission to space
 The backstory:
 SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission lifted off from Florida around 7:04 a.m Tuesday morning, carrying 32 payloads, including "cubesats, microsats, and reentry vehicles."
 The Source: The information used in this story was gathered from SpaceX's website and social media accounts, as well as viewer photos shared with FOX 35.
